English.Char_Desc_2000:
TranscribeGeek turns audio and video recordings into text on your own machine.
Drop files in, pick a model and a language, and press Transcribe. Each file gets a plain text transcript written beside it, with or without timestamps, and a SubRip SRT subtitle file too if you want one. Supported input includes WAV, MP3, M4A, FLAC, OGG, Opus, WMA, AAC, MP4, MKV, MOV, AVI and WebM.
It runs OpenAI Whisper models locally through whisper.cpp. There is no account, no server and no upload, the recording never leaves the computer it is on. There is no per-minute cap, no monthly allowance and no trial.
New in 1.1: TranscribeGeek can work out who is speaking. Tick the option and each line is labelled Speaker 1, Speaker 2 and so on, numbered in the order the voices are first heard, and you can tell it how many people are on the recording if you know. That needs a 36 MB speaker pack from the Models screen, which is checked against a SHA-256 recorded inside the application before it is kept. It is a good guess rather than a certainty, and the application says so on screen instead of pretending otherwise.
Four Whisper model sizes are offered, from 78 MB to 1.5 GB, and none of them are bundled into the installer: you pick one on the Models screen and it is fetched once and kept. 22 languages are supported, plus automatic language detection.
TranscribeGeek never overwrites your files. If a transcript of that name already exists, the next one is numbered. ffmpeg is used as a separate program for formats other than plain WAV and is deliberately not bundled.
Free to use, including at work. GPL-3.0. No paid tier.
